name: stri_enc_mark
title: Get Declared Encodings of Each String

origin.description: Report the declared encoding mark of each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector. A raw vector is coerced with as.character first.

origin.details: ASCII means every byte is in 0..127. Anything else that is valid Unicode is UTF-8. NA stays missing. A raw vector becomes two-digit hex strings, which are ASCII.
origin.example:
x <- stri_enc_mark(c("abc", "\u0105"))
cat(paste0("stri_enc_mark(c(\"abc\", \"ą\")) returns ", paste(x, collapse = ", "), ".\n"))

translation.description: Report the declared encoding mark of each string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, NA, or a list of those. bytes are read as two-digit hex strings, the way as.character treats a raw vector.

translation.details: ASCII means every code point is in 0..127. Any other Python text is UTF-8. NA stays missing. The text "NA" is ASCII.
translation.value: A string, NA, or a list of those.
translation.example:
from stringi.encoding import stri_enc_mark
x = stri_enc_mark(["abc", "ą"])
print("stri_enc_mark([\"abc\", \"ą\"]) returns " + ", ".join(x) + ".")
